decisions.decision: Serve fraud scores through a queue-fronted online cluster
decisions.context: Authorization requires a score within tens of milliseconds, including during transaction peaks.
decisions.rationale: The queue-fronted cluster distributes online predictors for throughput and low latency, which fits authorization-time scoring better than scheduled batch output (Architecting a Machine Learning Pipeline: How to build scalable Machine Learning systems - Part 2/2; System Architectures for Personalization and Recommendation). The checked design point had no warnings, though no source attested to the full combination.
consequences: Operate a queue and multiple predictors.
Set capacity and overload behavior to meet the latency target.

decisions.decision: Expose predictions through a REST microservice
decisions.context: The payment authorization path needs a request-response interface to obtain a transaction score from an independently operated model.

alternatives.label: gRPC model interface
cons: Fewer sources in this design space

decisions.rationale: A REST prediction microservice provides a clear application integration boundary, while the brief does not require a particular transport optimization. Sources describe REST-backed model prediction services (How to power up your product by machine learning with python microservice, pt. 1; Architecting a Machine Learning Pipeline: How to build scalable Machine Learning systems - Part 2/2).
consequences: Keep request and response schemas versioned.
Measure end-to-end latency, including feature lookup and network time.

decisions.decision: Deploy the scorer as a model-as-a-service
decisions.context: Transaction scoring must remain available as traffic changes, with the model deployable independently from payment application code.
decisions.rationale: A real-time model service integrates with product applications and supports a separate deployment boundary suited to scaling the scorer for peaks (Productionizing Machine Learning with a Microservices Architecture; MLOps: Continuous delivery and automation pipelines in machine learning).
consequences: Operate and scale the serving service separately.
Coordinate compatibility between model and caller versions.

decisions.decision: Track model, feature, and training lineage end to end
decisions.context: Auditors must be able to identify the exact model version and features behind each score after the transaction.

alternatives.label: Artifact version control
cons: Does not cover full training lineage

decisions.rationale: This choice includes versioned artifacts, training runs, metadata, deployment health, and datasets, providing a stronger basis for answering auditors than artifact versioning alone (Continuous Intelligence: Moving Machine Learning Application into Production Reliably; MLOps Principles). The checked design point had no warnings, though no source attested to the full combination.
consequences: Persist the model version and feature-set identifiers with each score.
Retain lineage metadata for the audit period.

decisions.decision: Monitor service health and input quality in production
decisions.context: Peak traffic and strict response times make operational failures visible risks; changing transaction data can also degrade scores.
decisions.rationale: This monitoring covers latency, uptime, dependencies, input quality, and data shifts, directly addressing the brief’s operational constraints. Real-time quality checks can complement it when labels become available; monitoring practices are combinable in this dimension (Productionizing Machine Learning with a Microservices Architecture; MLOps Principles).
consequences: Alert on latency, availability, dependency, and input-quality breaches.
Decide separately how label delays affect model-quality alerts.

uncovered: How transaction features are computed and served within the latency budget.
How to explain individual fraud scores and preserve the exact feature values used for each decision.
Fraud-label delay, retraining approval, and rollback policy.
Authorization behavior when the scorer or feature dependencies are unavailable.
